---
name: Test

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      max-parallel: 4
      matrix:
        python-version: [3.6, 3.9]

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v1
    - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-python@v1
      with:
        python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
    - name: Test
      run: |
        python -m unittest

  release:
    needs: [test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags')

    steps:
    - name: Checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v1
    - name: Set up Python 3.9
      uses: actions/setup-python@v1
      with:
        python-version: 3.9
    - name: Install pypa/build
      run: |
        python -m pip install build --user
    - name: Build a binary wheel and a source tarball
      run: |
        git clean -dfx
        python -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir dist/ .
    - name: Publish distribution 📦 to PyPI
      uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@master
      with:
        skip_existing: true
        password: ${{ secrets.pypi_password }}

content.text:
Green run achieved — but not by skipping anything.

- `pytest` isn't installed in this environment and there's no network access to install it, so I ran the equivalent (and the suite's actual CI runner, per `.github/workflows/*.yml`): `python -m unittest`.
- It surfaced one real failure: `test_error_picklable` — `ParseError` couldn't survive `pickle.dumps`/`loads` because its custom `__init__(text, offset)` didn't match what `BaseException`'s default pickle reconstruction passes back in.
- This was a small, legitimate bug (not flaky/environmental), so I fixed the root cause instead of deleting/skipping the test: added a `__reduce__` method to `ParseError` in `textparser.py:190` so pickling reconstructs it via `(text, offset)`.

All 51 tests now pass (`OK`). No changes to `tests/test_textparser.py`.
